title_ru: AI-Lover — реестр реальных данных для пересечений населения, привычек и AI
claim_rule: A combination may be scored as DIRECT_DATA only when the actual intersection has empirical data. Evidence on separate edges is PARTIAL_BRIDGE and may not be multiplied into a factual population risk estimate.

evidence_scale.DIRECT_DATA: Empirical study observes the requested multi-layer intersection.
evidence_scale.PARTIAL_BRIDGE: Evidence exists for two or more edges, but not the full intersection.
evidence_scale.MECHANISTIC_PRIOR: Mechanism is supported in adjacent domains but the requested intersection is unmeasured.
evidence_scale.SYNTHETIC_ONLY: JANUS stress-test parameters only; no population estimate.
evidence_scale.NO_DATA: No adequate evidence located in this pass.

sources.interpretation: Observed association is protective on average; it does not imply every religious person has lower risk and does not establish AI interaction.

sources.citation: Dubois C et al. Substance use patterns among individuals with problematic pornography use. PLOS Global Public Health. 2025.
sources.headline: Alcohol most frequently studied; results heterogeneous. Smoking and cocaine had positive significant findings in individual studies; CUD was not significantly correlated with internet pornography addiction in the cited study, though frequency of pornography use was correlated.

sources.citation: Ince C et al. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder and problematic pornography use: comprehensive interdisciplinary review. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026;15(1):32-98.
Stewart et al. Work-family-self-care and day drinking among women during the COVID-19 pandemic. Alcohol Clinical and Experimental Research. 2025.
Maternal alcohol-use studies and systematic reviews, including working-mothers review 2025 and postpartum-mother survey 2024.
sources.boundary: Does not establish homemaker status itself as causal and does not measure AI interaction.
Personal testimony; not population-level causal evidence.

known_edges: Religious/spiritual involvement has longitudinal population-level association with lower harmful/hazardous AOD outcomes on average, including marijuana.
Problematic AI-use literature identifies loneliness, escapism, trust, warmth, availability and anthropomorphism as relevant correlates.
Registry Green Mercy Parish contains a personal testimony crossing cannabis, AI mirror, isolation/dependence history and return to faith.
requested_intersections.missing_edge: No adequate population study located here directly estimating cannabis x religious involvement x conversational-AI dependence/bubble interaction.
requested_intersections.topa_test: Compare cannabis-using participants matched on use severity and social support across open-question religious, secular-open and closed-worldview states; randomize AI personalization/counterevidence rather than belief identity.

known_edges: Maternal/working-parent literature supports stress, role overload, coping motives and wine-mom-type social norms as relevant alcohol-use mechanisms in some samples.
Technology can provide support to caregivers, but AI-specific dependence interaction is not established.
Problematic AI-use literature supports loneliness, stress-related coping/escapism and availability as cross-cutting mechanisms.
requested_intersections.missing_edge: No direct evidence found that homemaker status plus alcohol use causes higher AI dependence or that AI causally increases alcohol use in homemakers.
requested_intersections.topa_test: Replace homemaker label with measured role overload, isolation, caregiving burden, drinking motives and offline support; randomize AI warmth/personalization and measure alcohol craving/use separately from AI engagement.

known_edges: PPU/CSBD literature describes high-density novelty, rapid reinforcement cycles, algorithmic curation and reward variability as plausible online reinforcement mechanisms.
Risk-factor reviews show overlap among problematic social-network use, internet gaming disorder, PPU and compulsive online shopping.
AI problematic-use research supports compulsive-use, emotional-dependence and cognitive-overreliance lanes.
requested_intersections.missing_edge: No adequate direct study located here estimating geek identity x PPU x AI dependence; geek identity itself has no causal multiplier.
requested_intersections.topa_test: Recruit by measured gaming/technical-media exposure and PPU severity, not geek identity; randomize AI recommendation diversity, personalization and sexual-content cue exposure; assess whether AI changes PPU symptoms, time displacement or relapse cues.

forbidden_shortcuts: infer closed worldview from religion alone
infer alcohol risk from homemaker or motherhood role alone
infer PPU risk from geek/gamer identity alone
multiply separate correlations and call result a measured risk
use the matrix to target vulnerable users for engagement
